rules: Every key is checked: a key the fields do not name is an error, not ignored.
Write format daggerheart-loot/lists and version 3; the import also reads versions 1 and 2.
An entry id is a catalog record id (search_catalog, get_record); an id the catalog does not hold is skipped and named, and the rest of the file imports.
Leave a key out for its default: quantity 1, an empty note, no price.
An entry with source homebrew names a homebrew key; its snapshot is a copy that an export writes. Write catalog entries unless you copy them from an export.

fields.note: The URL of this schema, for editors. Ignored on import.
Names the file as a lists file.
The format version this schema describes.
When the site wrote the file. Ignored on import.
The lists, each imported as a new account list, in this order.
The list's name, in Unicode code points.
How the list shows prices: in bags or in coins. See "Money" in llms.txt.
The list's note that players may read through a share link.
The list's note that only the GM reads.
The list's entries in list order; an empty array for an empty list.
A record id from catalog.csv; for source homebrew, the item key (hb_ and 16 characters of a-z and 2-7). A catalog id the site does not know is skipped on import.
The record's name, for a person reading the file. Ignored on import.

official for a catalog record; homebrew for a GM's own item, by its key. An account that holds the key gets a link to its item; any other gets an own copy made from snapshot, or skips an entry without one.
How many of the record the list holds.
The price in whole coins, whatever the money mode; leave the key out for no price. See "Money" in llms.txt.
The entry's note that players may read through a share link.
The entry's note that only the GM reads.
true: the entry is «Только для мастера» (GM only) - a players' share link leaves it out, the GM's link shows it. The export writes it only as true; leave it out for an entry the players see.

A homebrew item as the catalog draws it: the item's fields with its key as id, each name and description filled from the other language when it lacks one, its source with the section, and the set card and rule cards of its author it names. tier is the loot tier, or A on equipment only when eq.tier is A. A snapshot passes only whole: write it from the item, never by hand.
